Tomato_Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked leaf spots that may develop yellow margins; spots can also appear on stems and fruit.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterial infection, often spread by splashing water, contaminated tools, and infected planting material.
organic_treatment: Remove badly affected leaves and dispose of them away from the crop.
Avoid handling plants while they are wet and disinfect tools between plants.
prevention: Use clean seed and healthy transplants.
Rotate away from tomato and related crops where practical.
Water at the base of plants and improve airflow.

Tomato_Early_blight.symptoms: Brown leaf spots, often with concentric rings, usually beginning on older lower leaves; affected leaves may yellow and fall.
Tomato_Early_blight.cause: Fungal infection that persists in crop debris and spreads in warm, wet conditions.
organic_treatment: Remove affected lower leaves and crop debris.
Use mulch to reduce soil splash and keep foliage dry when watering.
prevention: Rotate crops and remove volunteer tomato plants.
Space plants to improve airflow and avoid overhead watering.

Tomato_Late_blight.symptoms: Fast-spreading, water-soaked dark lesions on leaves and stems; white growth may appear on leaf undersides in humid conditions.
Tomato_Late_blight.cause: Late blight pathogen favored by cool, humid weather and spread by wind and water.
organic_treatment: Remove and safely dispose of infected plants promptly to limit spread.
Keep foliage dry and seek local extension advice when symptoms spread quickly.
prevention: Inspect crops frequently during cool, wet weather.
Use healthy planting material, allow airflow, and avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale or yellow patches on upper leaf surfaces with olive-green to brown growth underneath, often in humid conditions.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.cause: Fungal infection favored by high humidity and poor airflow, especially under cover.
organic_treatment: Remove heavily affected leaves and improve ventilation around plants.
Reduce leaf wetness and avoid crowding.
prevention: Water at the base of plants and remove infected crop debris.

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small, round spots with pale centers and dark edges, usually starting on lower leaves; affected leaves may yellow and drop.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.cause: Fungal infection that survives on crop debris and spreads by rain splash and handling wet plants.
organic_treatment: Remove affected lower leaves and dispose of crop debris.
Mulch soil to limit splash and avoid working among wet plants.
prevention: Rotate crops and keep volunteer tomato plants under control.
Water at the base and leave enough space between plants.

Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.symptoms: Fine pale stippling on leaves, bronzing, and sometimes fine webbing, especially on leaf undersides during hot, dry conditions.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.cause: Feeding by spider mites, which can multiply rapidly in hot, dry weather.
organic_treatment: Remove heavily infested leaves and monitor leaf undersides regularly.
Reduce dust and water-stress; protect naturally occurring beneficial insects.
prevention: Scout crops regularly, especially during hot, dry periods.
Avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum pesticide use that can harm mite predators.

Tomato__Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown circular leaf lesions with concentric rings; spots may also affect stems and fruit.
Tomato__Target_Spot.cause: Fungal infection favored by warm, humid conditions and prolonged leaf wetness.
organic_treatment: Remove affected leaves and crop debris.
Improve airflow and avoid wetting foliage when watering.
prevention: Use crop rotation and healthy transplants.
Space plants well and reduce leaf wetness.

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward-curling leaves, yellowing, stunted growth, and reduced fruit set; symptoms are often strongest on new growth.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.cause: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus, commonly spread by whiteflies.
prevention: Use healthy transplants and protect young plants from whiteflies.
Control weeds that can host whiteflies and monitor plants frequently.
management_steps: Remove and dispose of severely infected plants to reduce sources of virus.
Manage whiteflies using physical and cultural controls and seek local extension guidance.
Do not treat the virus as curable; protect healthy plants from further spread.

Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green leaves, leaf distortion, and stunted growth; fruit may ripen unevenly.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Tomato mosaic virus, which spreads through infected plant material and contaminated hands or tools.
prevention: Use healthy seed and transplants and clean tools between plants.
Wash hands after handling suspected infected plants and remove crop debris.
management_steps: Remove and dispose of infected plants; there is no curative treatment.
Clean tools and wash hands after handling plants to limit mechanical spread.
Avoid saving seed from affected plants.

Tomato_healthy.message: No tomato disease was identified. Continue checking plants regularly for changes.
general_care_tips: Water at the base of plants and avoid keeping leaves wet.
Maintain space between plants for airflow.
Remove crop debris and check leaves regularly, including their undersides.
